author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
`ThemeValidator` was a stateless namespace — one public `validate` method over roughly fifteen private helpers, plus a field holding constant defaults. The instance existed only to group functions.

The conversion is an inversion rather than a rewrite, because the function form already existed and was already the public API:

```ts
export function validateTheme(theme: ThemeConfig, options?: ValidationOptions): ValidationResult {
  const validator = new ThemeValidator()
  // ...
}
```

Both real consumers — `ThemeProvider.tsx:211` and `NativeThemeProvider.tsx:190` — call `validateTheme`. Nothing in production ever constructed the class. So the helpers move to module scope, `validateTheme` becomes the implementation, and the wrapper goes away.

## Removing the export

`ThemeValidator` was exported from the package barrel, which would normally be breaking. `@sparkle/theme` is at `0.0.0` and has never been published — `npm view @sparkle/theme` returns 404 — so there are no consumers to break.

Deleted outright rather than left as a deprecated adapter. #2013 removed one of those from `moo-dang` for being pure indirection, and adding a new one here would repeat the pattern this codebase just cleaned up.

`validateTheme` and `isValidTheme` are unchanged and still exported.

## Behavior

Identical. Options thread through to the helpers explicitly instead of via instance state; no validation rule, error message, or `ValidationResult` shape changed.

The test file is the safety net for that claim. It went from 49 assertions to 48 — the single removal being `expect(validator).toBeInstanceOf(ThemeValidator)`, which tested implementation rather than behavior. Every remaining assertion is unchanged; the only edits are mechanical `validator.validate(...)` → `validateTheme(...)` swaps.

Removes the `no-restricted-syntax` suppression added in #2015, which read: [description truncated to fit budget]
title: refactor(theme): convert ThemeValidator to module-scope functions
